bottom_line: Wall Street had a rough day even though Anthropic, the AI company that makes Claude, pulled off a record stock market debut. The bigger weight on stocks is the Fed, the people who set interest rates: they are openly talking about raising rates because prices are still rising too fast.

stories.title: Big IPO, but stocks still fell
stories.real: The Dow dropped about 1,100 points and closed below 50,000 for the first time since June, and the Nasdaq fell more than 2%. The S&P 500 is on its longest losing streak since June, and the selling spread to Asia, where SoftBank fell over 16%.

stories.title: The Fed is leaning toward hikes
stories.real: Several Fed officials, including Goolsbee and Paulson, back raising rates, and Fed minutes say higher rates are needed in December. Goolsbee says inflation is 'way higher' than the Fed's 2% target, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings. Officials agree on going up but disagree on how fast.
stories.you: When the Fed raises rates, credit cards, car loans and mortgages usually get more expensive, and savings accounts usually pay a bit more.

stories.title: Anthropic's record stock debut
stories.real: Anthropic raised more than $100B in its IPO, the first time a company sells shares to the public. It jumped 27% on day one to a $1.8 trillion market value. It is the first purely AI company to go public, and analysts warn the shares could swing a lot in the coming weeks.
stories.you: A brand-new stock can move up or down hard in its first weeks, so the opening-day pop says little about where it ends up.

stories.title: Chip makers under China scrutiny
stories.real: California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia in a probe into AI chips ending up in China, after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. A congressman says Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. AMD fell over 7% after a short seller, someone who profits when a stock falls, claimed its firmware showed up at a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law.
stories.you: Many index funds hold a lot of Nvidia and AMD, so legal trouble at these companies can show up in ordinary retirement accounts.

stories.title: Gold and the dollar move
stories.real: Gold fell below $3,650 and is headed for its worst week in eight months. Expected Fed hikes are making the U.S. dollar stronger, which pushes gold down and puts pressure on the euro.
stories.you: If you own gold, it has had a bad week, and a strong dollar makes foreign trips and imported goods cheaper for Americans.
